title: Securing a server using AI
partialText: I asked Codex to audit a freshly migrated Ubuntu server. It enabled the firewall, hardened SSH and Apache, removed installer files, applied 124 security updates and rebooted. Here is what it found and what I learned.

title: How I fixed my DevOps mistakes with AI
partialText: I resized a DigitalOcean droplet the wrong way and locked myself into a $48/month plan. Codex migrated my Sendy server to a new $12 droplet over SSH, database included, while I changed DNS.

title: The complete guide to Codex
partialText: How to use Codex, OpenAI's coding agent: the desktop app from first prompt to review, then the CLI, skills, plugins, worktrees, and scheduled tasks.

title: Debugging a process killed on my server with Codex
partialText: Claude Code kept dying a few seconds after starting on my Ubuntu server. I pointed Codex CLI at the server over SSH and it found the Linux OOM killer in the kernel logs. Here is the whole session.

title: Merchant of Record or payment processor? How to choose how to get paid online
partialText: The first payment decision most guides skip: sell through a Merchant of Record like Creem or Paddle, or stay the merchant with Stripe? What each one handles, what it costs, and how to choose.

title: Where to host your web app: how to choose
partialText: Compare static hosts, serverless platforms, PaaS options, and VPS providers using current prices, limits, database needs, and operational tradeoffs.

title: What I learned in the past 6 months about using agentic AI
partialText: Six months of building with coding agents every day. Where the bottleneck moved, what I stopped doing, and the habits that survived contact with real projects.

title: Software was never worth the hours it took
partialText: AI can compress months of development into days. The cost of producing software is falling, but its value was never a tally of engineering hours.

title: When more people are building software, what's the value of software?
partialText: AI is making software cheaper to create. That does not make software worthless, but it changes what people will pay for and where builders need to create value.

title: How to make AI harnesses talk less
partialText: Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor write too much? Turn on concise output styles, hide reasoning summaries, and write short output rules that stick.

title: A deep dive into tldraw
partialText: A practical guide to tldraw: the infinite canvas, React SDK, AI integrations, local agent workflows, Flash animations, and software development use cases.

title: Understanding tsconfig.json
partialText: Understand tsconfig.json options that matter: strict, target, lib, module resolution, noEmit, paths, include, and a modern starter configuration.

title: How to use Cursor Projects
partialText: Cursor Projects gives you a coordinator agent that plans work, delegates it to subagents, keeps shared context, and watches your PRs. Here is how to use it.

title: JSONL: a practical guide to JSON Lines
partialText: Learn how JSONL stores one JSON value per line, how to write, stream, and query it, and why I use it as Factory Log's event store.

title: A deep dive into Ghostty
partialText: Ghostty from scratch: install it, learn the shortcuts, write the config, pick fonts and themes, use splits, build keybindings, set up shell integration and SSH.

title: AI and the joy of programming
partialText: AI made me more productive than I've ever been, but the way building software feels has changed. Some honest thoughts on where the joy went.

title: I updated ahastack.dev for htmx 4
partialText: ahastack.dev now runs on Astro 7 and htmx 4, has 18 live demos on Cloudflare, and ships a skill file so coding agents know how to build with the AHA stack.

title: Native email and password authentication on Cloudflare Workers
partialText: Build native email/password auth on Cloudflare Workers with peppered PBKDF2 hashes, D1 sessions, and hardened HttpOnly cookies.

title: A deep dive into tmux
partialText: Learn tmux from scratch: create persistent sessions, use windows and panes, copy text, customize key bindings, and work safely over SSH.

title: My software is now on GitHub
partialText: The eight packages in my software catalog are now public MIT repositories on GitHub, with the full source, tests, and documentation in one README each.

title: I launched CLI Tools
partialText: CLI Tools is a free, open source macOS app that catalogs every command-line tool you installed with Homebrew, npm, and Cargo, with examples, shell history, and a JSON CLI for coding agents.

title: The Cloudflare products I actually use
partialText: An honest report on the Cloudflare products I use in real projects, what each one solves, the gotchas I found, and what I do not use yet.

title: Why I think more clearly when I type
partialText: Typing is slower than speaking, but that friction helps me develop ideas, notice weak sentences, and turn rough thoughts into useful writing.

title: I launched Things CLI
partialText: Things CLI is a free command-line tool for creating, reading, and updating Things 3 projects and tasks from the terminal or a coding agent.

title: Build a language model on your Mac with Language Model Builder
partialText: Language Model Builder teaches how LLMs work and lets you train a small GPT locally on an Apple Silicon Mac, without writing code.

title: Why your MacBook runs hotter at high altitude
partialText: MacBooks run hotter above 1800 meters because thin air carries away less heat. Learn the physics behind it and simple ways to keep your laptop cool.

title: Vercel AI Gateway tutorial
partialText: Use Vercel AI Gateway with the AI SDK and OpenAI client, then add model routing, fallbacks, caching, budgets, BYOK, and observability.

title: How AI agents can log in without seeing your passwords
partialText: Compare 1Password Agentic Autofill, Bitwarden's Agent Access SDK, Browser Use sensitive data, OAuth token vaults, and why passkeys still block AI agents.

title: A deep dive into exe.dev
partialText: exe.dev gives you persistent Linux VMs over SSH, each with an HTTPS URL, private-by-default sharing, and a built-in coding agent. How it works, what it costs, and how I use it.

title: Zustand: simple React state management
partialText: Learn Zustand through a React store: actions, selectors, immutable updates, persistence, testing, SSR boundaries, and when local or server state is better.
